title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-21
taper: Recorded by Ken & Judy Lee on a Sony pc-124 cassette deck with Sony dynamic mics on Norelco cassettes. Microphones were set up in the balcony with a 10-20 foot spread.

ai_review.summary: Clear audience tape captures a fiery March 1970 show featuring an epic 18‑minute Dancin' jam, the debut of Friend of the Devil and a soaring Midnight Hour → Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The late‑show from March 21‑1970 is praised for its high‑energy performance – a monster Dancin' improvisation, rare early versions of Friend of the Devil, Walking The Dog and He Was A Friend Of Mine, plus an inspired acoustic set that rolls into a blistering Midnight Hour → Lovelight.  While the audience recording isn’t a soundboard, listeners note it is surprisingly clear and lively, though occasional cuts and noisy crowd moments are evident.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rave about the musical performance and cite rare/first‑time songs; recording is described as clear and enjoyable despite minor cuts, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and crisp for a 1970 audience tape; several reviewers call it "nice and clear".  Some note occasional cuts (e.g., Easy Wind ending) and sections of loud audience noise, but overall the tape is listenable.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: The early set packs rare folk‑rock material and surprise covers, followed by an expansive acoustic segment that segues into a high‑octane second half with long jams and a powerful close.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for perfect tone and flawless lead work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for creative, melodic bass lines especially during the Dancin' jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for an outstanding solo on Easy Wind and strong vocal contributions.
